npnjs.com phishing backdoored npm packages

Campaign: npnjs-scam-npm-2025
Date: 2025-07-18 to 2025-07-22 (4 days)
Actor: Third Party (group)
Impact: code_execution, credential_theft, remote_access

Synopsis

The npnjs.com campaign used a lookalike npm login domain to phish maintainers and publish malicious releases across JavaScript tooling packages in July 2025.

Story

The campaign began with a letter off by one character. Maintainers were sent to `npnjs.com`, a lookalike of the npm login flow, and the stolen credentials became publish rights.

The attacker used those rights to ship malicious npm versions under real package names. Some packages added install-time scripts and downloader logic; others carried backdoors or credential theft. The registry was not broken. The accounts were.

The first visible cluster centered on ESLint and Prettier tooling, then expanded to other maintainers and packages using the same phishing infrastructure. That made the campaign larger than any single package compromise while still preserving package-level dates and versions.

Its impact landed on developer workstations and CI systems. JavaScript install hooks run at the edge of trust: after dependency resolution, before review, often inside environments rich with tokens.
